issue.title: tool/monitor/proc show -F followers drop or skip output when a bounded log rotates; use ProcLogCursor
issue.description:
Found by the sase-17p land agent (2026-09-24, master 682089c84) while integrating epic
sase-17p with work that landed during it.

Bounded proc/monitor logs rotate: src/sase/logs/_bounded.py `_rotate_if_needed_locked`
does `os.replace(path, path.with_name(path.name + ".1"))` once an append would exceed
max_bytes (DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES = 2 MiB; SASE_PROC_LOG_MAX_BYTES overrides for procs). The
CLI log followers track only a byte offset:

- `sase tool show RUN -F` — src/sase/tool/query.py `_stream_output_paths` (added by
  sase-17p.4 df8ed5134): `if size < start: start = 0`.
- `sase monitor show ID -F` — src/sase/main/monitor/show.py `_read_new_text`: same reset.
- `sase proc show ID -F` — src/sase/main/proc_handler.py `_follow_log` via
  `wait_for_proc(on_line=...)`; check whether it has the same shape.

When the log rotates between two polls, the bytes appended to the old file after the
last read (now in `<log>.1`) are silently dropped, and the new file is replayed from 0.
If the new file has already grown past the old offset by the next poll, no shrink is
seen, so the follower silently skips the new file's head too. No lost-bytes notice is
printed either way. A long `just check` or `check-full` run streamed through a verify
monitor can cross 2 MiB.

sase-17x.6 (70afac517) added `sase.procs.logs.ProcLogCursor`: an (inode, offset)
cursor that detects rotation, drains `<name>.1` from the held offset, and reports
`lost_bytes`. It already takes an explicit `log_path`, so it works for monitor
`live_reply.md` logs and ToolRun owner logs. Today only the TUI Command Line uses it.

Fix: route all three CLI followers through ProcLogCursor, looping `read_new()` until it
returns empty each poll (it caps each read at 64 KiB). Print a one-line stderr notice
when `lost_bytes > 0`. Add rotation tests with a small max_bytes: an append crosses the
limit between two polls and every byte is streamed exactly once.

task_type_fields.impact: Anyone following a long run's output live (agents' follow-ups, humans watching check-full) can miss log lines, silently, including failure output near a rotation boundary.
task_type_fields.repro: Set SASE_PROC_LOG_MAX_BYTES small (e.g. 4096), hand off 'sase tool run -H -- sh -c "for i in $(seq 2000); do echo line-$i; sleep 0.001; done"', and follow it with 'sase tool show RUN -F' (or 'sase monitor show ID -F' for a monitor): lines around each rotation go missing and no lost-bytes notice is printed.
